citations.narrative:
During the facilities walk-through, there were four enclosures with an excessive amount of flies both covering and flying
around the food (fruit) of the porcupines contained within. There were male and female pairs in each of the enclosures,
which included four African Crested Porcupines and two Indian Crested Porcupines — of which you could hear the
swarming sound from the flies.
Failing to maintain an effective pest control program can result in insects congregating around food sources/animal areas,
adversely affecting sanitation and increasing the potential for contamination or attraction of additional pests, all of which
could negatively impact the health and well-being of the animals. A safe and effective program for the control of insects,
ectoparasites, and avian and mammalian pests shall be established and maintained.
Correct by: October 12, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensees.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
